name: Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport
before:
Fujian's main airport, on the north side of Xiamen Island and only 10 km from downtown, which makes it one of the more convenient arrivals in coastal China. It is the hub for XiamenAir and for TAECO, a large aircraft maintenance operation.

The terminal numbering catches people out. Terminal 1 was demolished in 2012 and Terminal 2 became the domestic area of Terminal 3, so a client told to go to Terminal 2 is looking for part of another building. Terminal 4 was completed in 2014.

The airport has an unusual history. It was built by Japan during the occupation, converted to civilian use after the surrender, then left largely abandoned through the 1950s because of shelling risk from Kinmen just offshore. It reopened properly in 1983 with funding from the Kuwait Fund, and traffic grew quickly enough after that to need three new terminals inside twenty years.
after:
Xiamen's airport, on the north side of Xiamen Island and only 10 km from downtown, which makes it one of the more convenient arrivals in coastal China.

Its days are numbered. The new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport is expected to open by the end of 2026 and take over all of Gaoqi's passenger and cargo flights, so check which airport a client will use for any trip from late 2026.

Until then, the terminal numbering can catch people out: the old Terminal 2 has been turned into part of Terminal 3, so a client told to go to Terminal 2 is looking for part of another building.

claims.note: New in the text, and the most important thing about this airport now: the old text did not mention the move. The Beijing News (6 July 2026) says Xiang'an was in its final push and expected to open by the end of this year, taking over all Gaoqi's passenger and cargo business; Wikipedia says Gaoqi will stop all civilian flights once Xiang'an opens. No exact date was found.
